title: Passing points on driveways serving five or more dwellings
text: Driveways designed to allow vehicles to pass in opposite directions where it serves five or more dwellings. Passing points are to be provided at least every 30m with driveways to be minimum 5.5m wide for a minimum 6.3m length (excluding manoeuvring tapers) (refer Figure 3.7c).

replaces.note: Part B 4 m continuous width for 5+ dwellings -> 3 m driveway with 5.5 m passing points; Part B C5.6 retained-dwelling reduction is now merit M3.7.3

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 3 - Grouped Dwellings.pdf

notes: diverges: clause number reused. Chapter 3 C3.7.5 (p41) is new to the grouped package (passing points); Chapter 2 C3.7.5 is the sightline truncation, which is Chapter 3 C3.7.7. Trigger is the dwelling count only (proposed fact parking.driveway.dwellings_served); the text sets no driveway-length trigger, '30 m' is the maximum spacing of passing points. The applicant's yes/no (site.communal_street_passing_bay) covers spacing at least every 30 m and a 5.5 m width for 6.3 m length excluding tapers (Figure 3.7c). The same fact answers C3.7.6.

verified.note: Five or more dwellings, 30m spacing, 5.5m x 6.3m (tapers excluded) confirmed. The yes/no site.communal_street_passing_bay is shared with C3.7.6, which tests a different provision (5.5m for 6.3m from the street boundary on an arterial); where both apply one answer covers both.
